narrative.northStar: The Keynote Stage in season liveries, after McLaren (rounds 8 and 9)
narrative.overview:
Each season's robot is launched the way a hardware company launches a product: the machine alone on an almost-black stage, lit from above, standing on a thin floor line. Then the page steps out into calm white and aluminium-grey reading pages that explain the robot, the people, the outreach and the partners.

**Season liveries (round 9; Andy: "reference the mclaren page and build more interactive and somewhat colorful page").** Every FTC season has a game, and FIRST gives each game a colour palette. Each season wears its game's colour wherever that season is shown: its bay on the home stage, its card, its row on the Seasons page, its page head, its pager and its tag in the record. This season's colour is also the site's one signal colour, the way a racing team repaints its livery each year: the sponsor action, the tag above section headings, the next event in the calendar, the controls that move things. McLaren uses its papaya the same way (measured on mclaren.com/racing/formula-1: about 1.5% of the screen, in solid blocks, thin bars and arrows, never behind reading text). Beyond that, colour still comes only from the robots, the photos, the Mercury logo (kept as-is) and, on the partners page, the four sponsorship tiers in the colours of their names (Andy, 2026-11-09: "the sponsorship category should be the color of the tier name"); the budget donut is grey.

Two grounds carry the site. The stage (home launch, every season head, the partners package sheet (head, tier chart and budget donut), and the closing "join or partner" bands on the home, team and partners pages) and the reading ground (white, with aluminium-grey bands). Sections run the full width of the page and are separated by a change of ground, never by hairlines. Since round 7 (Andy: "reference the VulcanForms website") the things inside a section are boxes drawn like the cells of an engineering spec sheet: white, a 1px #C4C3CC line and near-square 6px corners (Stage Step with a light line on the stage). Nothing floats: the rounded panels on a grey ground from round 6 were removed because Andy said they looked "so AI". Buttons are pills, and nothing casts a shadow except a robot on its floor (the only other shadows are the small lift under the chosen outreach year and the halo around the part markers). One family, Archivo, does everything; robot names are set extra wide (125%).

The neutrals are our own: tinted from the logo's dark outline, not copied. The reference study of Apple, TechCrunch, Vogue, The New York Times Company and Prada specifically warned against reusing Apple's exact greys (#F5F5F7, #A1A1A6) and its 28px cards, which is why the values and radii here differ.
keyCharacteristics: Two grounds: the near-black stage for launches and closing calls, white and aluminium grey for reading.

Season liveries: each season wears its game's colour (from FIRST's style guide for that game), and this season's colour is the one signal colour, always in solid blocks with an ink keyline. Robots, photos and the logo carry the rest; the four sponsorship tiers wear the colour of their names; the budget donut is grey.

Archivo only: page and section headings in capitals at 108% width and 700 (a lighter second line where the heading has a natural one), 125% width at 700 for robot and game names, sentence-case nav and text links, tabular figures for every number.

Full-width sections; every item (a write-up, a member, a program, a season, a post, a table, a tile) is a white box with a 1px line and square corners. Square buttons, no section hairlines, no shadows (except the floating header bar once the page scrolls, and the open menu).
Selection shown as light: the chosen bay's field is lit in its season's colour, the others hold a deep shade of theirs; a chosen story row turns white with a signal-colour marker.
One authored opening (the line-up title card, once a visit) and one load moment on the stage; everything else answers a click, tap, drag or key. Nothing moves, fades, pins or changes while scrolling.

rules.name: The Season Livery Rule
rules.body: A season's colour appears only where that season is shown, and the signal colour only at its fixed places (listed above). Colour is always a solid block, a bar, a tag or an arrow: never a page or section background behind reading text, never a tinted table column, never a gradient between two colours, never a new hue for links or highlights. Violet stays out (Andy found it AI-like).

rules.name: The Keyline Rule
rules.body: Every block of the signal colour carries an ink keyline (a 1.5px ink border or inset line), as the yellow shapes in the BIOBUZZ logo do. It keeps a light colour's edge clear on white (yellow on white is 1.3:1 without it) and is invisible on the stage. Season fields (bays, heads, rows) have no keyline: they are surfaces, not controls.

rules.name: The Light Still Leads Rule
rules.body: On the stage, emphasis is light: the chosen bay is lit, the others turned down. On light pages it is ink and weight; the signal colour marks actions and the current thing, never ordinary links or text.

rules.name: The Spec Box Rule
rules.body: Sections are full-width bands (white, aluminium or the stage); every inner page head is a stage band. Inside a section, each item is a box: paper fill, 1px `--box-line`, `--r-md` corners (0 since round 8), on white and aluminium bands alike; on the stage, Stage Step with a 1px light line (`--box-line-stage`). Inside a box, quotes, chips and photo frames are filled aluminium, never boxed again (css/style.css "Boxes"). The footer is a stage band that closes every page the way the header opens it.

rules.name: The Metals Name The Tiers Rule
rules.body: Each sponsorship tier wears the colour of its name, on its header block (ink text on it), the ticks in its column and its tag on a sponsor card. Nothing else on the site takes a metal: the column washes stay neutral, the budget donut stays grey, and text never wears one.

rules.name: The Width Is The Voice Rule
rules.body: Robot and game names go widest (125%, 700). Page and section headings go uppercase at 108%, in two weights where the heading has a natural first line. Reading text, nav and links stay at normal width in sentence case.

rules.name: The Fixed-Place Figures Rule
rules.body: Every date, amount, spec and result uses tabular lining figures (`<time>` and `.num` get them automatically; spec, facts, figures, budget and season-fact values set them).

rules.name: The Flat Tile Rule
rules.body: Boxes, menus and buttons never cast shadows, and a box never holds another box: inside a box, quotes, chips and photo frames take a flat aluminium fill instead.

dos: Do change colours, sizes, radii and spacing in `:root` in `css/style.css`, never in a component rule.
Do use the stage only for a launch (home, season heads), the partners head with its tier and budget sheet, and the closing call to join or partner; put everything else on paper or aluminium.
Do run sections the full width and put each item (a write-up, a member, a program, a season, a post, a table) in a white box with a 1px `--box-line` border, 6px corners and 16–24px padding.

Do keep every corner square, and end buttons and text links with the drawn arrow (none on mail links and submit buttons, a down arrow on downloads); use `.btn` on light and `.btn--light` / `.btn--outline-light` on the stage.

Do set robot and game names at 125% width and 700, page and section headings uppercase at 108% (split into two weights with `<span class="lite">` only where the heading has a natural first line), and everything else, nav and links included, at normal width in sentence case.
Do give every date, amount, spec and result tabular figures.
Do show a chosen state as light (brighter, full colour, filled dot) and write it to the URL when it is a view someone might share.
Do give a season its game's colour wherever that season is shown (`data-season`), and take that colour from FIRST's style guide for the game.
Do keep the signal colour to its fixed places, always as a solid block with an ink keyline and Stage Black text.
Do let the visitor drive anything that moves: buttons, drag, swipe, keys. Give every gesture a button and a key.
Do let new content simply be there: no entrance animation for anything below the first screen.
Do set `--w` to the image's pixel width on every `.photo`.
Do keep the sponsor strip in every footer, built from `SPONSORS` / `SUPPORTERS` in `js/main.js`.
Do add raster images only as the team's own photos or CAD renders, and record how any edited one was made (Assets and Provenance below).
donts: Don't add a hue beyond the season colours and the tier metals; no purple or violet accent, no neon on black.
Don't copy Apple's exact neutrals (#F5F5F7, #A1A1A6) or its 28px cards; use the tokens here.
Don't separate sections with hairlines; change the ground instead. Lines draw boxes and sit inside data, nowhere else.

Don't put shadows on boxes or buttons (the floating header bar's scrolled shadow and the open menu are the exceptions), round a corner, put a box inside a box, or float sections as rounded panels on a grey ground.

Don't colour the budget donut or tint the tier columns, and don't put a colour behind reading text or on pill-shaped controls (Andy, 2026-11-09, on colour mockups that did those things: "just dont do the color it looks terrible"). The tier metals he asked for later the same day; the season colours and the signal colour came with round 9, when he asked for a "somewhat colorful" site after McLaren's.
Don't add a second font family or system display faces.
Don't put small text labels (eyebrows) above headings or number the seasons 01/02/03; the 28×8px tag is the only mark above a heading, and it never goes on a heading inside a box.
Don't add new load animations outside the stage, counters that tick up, anything that moves by itself (a carousel that advances, a ticker), or motion that ignores reduced motion.
Don't generate or invent images, results, sponsors or numbers; leave "TBD" instead.
Don't show a photo larger than its own pixels.
